title: Who's Actually Faster?
covers: describing rates with two units, computing unit rates by dividing, and comparing speeds and unit prices
cert: finding unit rates by dividing and using them to compare speeds and prices

intro.caption: Lesson 3-2 — rates and unit rates. A Viper driver claims the fastest run because his total distance was longer. To settle it fairly, the crew needs meters per 1 minute.

balloons.t: 760 meters beats 600 meters! Is the Viper kart truly faster?
He drove for 4 minutes, Omar. I only ran for 3!
Different times! A rate compares two units, like meters and minutes.
To compare fairly, find the unit rate — meters per 1 minute.

pages.caption: You cannot compare raw totals when the times differ. Divide distance by time to get the unit rate.

balloons.t: Look for the word per. It tells you the amount for just ONE unit.
Divide my 600 meters by 3 minutes, and his 760 meters by 4 minutes.
Pack A is only $12! Pack B is $15! Clearly Pack A is cheaper!
Pack B has 6 boost cells, Omar. Check the unit price per cell.

sign.t:
Zara: 880 m in 4 min
Viper: 1,050 m in 5 min

balloons.t: Final qualifier logs are in! Let's see who has more meters per minute!
Numbers don't lie. Divide and call it!
220 meters per minute! Now let's rate these victory tacos per bite!

win.caption: A unit rate tells the amount for 1 unit. Divide to find meters per minute or dollars per item before you compare.

gates.title: Gate 1 · Rate Language
gates.badge: Unit Spotter — Rate vs. Unit Rate
gates.prompt: Pick out the true unit rate and explain why raw distance isn't enough.
hints: Conceptual: a unit rate always compares an amount to exactly 1 of another unit.
Procedural: look for 'per 1' or 'per' a single unit (like per minute or per item).

steps: 150 meters in 3 minutes is a rate, because it compares two different units (meters and minutes).
50 meters per minute is the unit rate — it is for just 1 minute.
worked.q: Which is a unit rate: 180 meters in 3 minutes, or 60 meters per minute?

options.fb: That is a rate for 3 minutes, not for 1 minute.
That is a single distance, not a rate comparing two units.
That is only a time, not a rate.

items.q: Why can't the Viper driver claim he is faster just because 760 meters > 600 meters?

options.fb: Even or odd numbers have nothing to do with speed.

options.t: Because they drove for different numbers of minutes
Because meters cannot be divided by minutes
options.fb: You divide meters by minutes to find speed.

options.t: Because the purple kart is heavier
options.fb: Weight does not change how you compare distance and time.

gates.pass: The Viper driver stops bragging. Time to divide.

gates.title: Gate 2 · Meters Per Minute
gates.prompt: Divide distance by minutes to find each kart's unit rate.
hints: Conceptual: speed in meters per minute means how many meters the kart goes in 1 minute.
Procedural: divide total meters by total minutes.

steps: The unit rate is 60 meters per minute.
worked.q: A kart goes 240 meters in 4 minutes. What is its speed in meters per minute?

items.label: Zara (600 m in 3 min) = ___ m/min
items.aria: Zara unit rate in meters per minute

fb.msg: That's 600 × 3. Divide distance by minutes instead.
300 is 600 ÷ 2. Zara ran for 3 minutes, not 2.

items.label: Viper (760 m in 4 min) = ___ m/min
items.aria: Viper unit rate in meters per minute

fb.msg: That's 760 − 4. Divide to get meters per 1 minute.

gates.pass: 200 m/min beats 190 m/min! Zara was faster all along.

gates.title: Gate 3 · Pit Shop Unit Price
gates.prompt: Find the unit price (cost per 1 cell) to pick the better buy.
hints: Conceptual: a lower total price is not always the better buy if you get fewer items.
Procedural: divide total dollars by the number of cells.

steps: $2 is less than $3, so Deal 2 is the better buy.
worked.q: 4 stickers cost $8. What is the unit price in dollars per sticker?

items.label: Pack B (6 cells for $15) = $___ per cell
items.aria: Pack B unit price in dollars per cell

fb.msg: That's 15 − 6. Divide cost by number of cells.
$3 is Pack A ($12 ÷ 4). Divide $15 by 6 for Pack B.

items.q: Pack A is 4 cells for $12 ($3.00 per cell). Pack B is 6 cells for $15 ($2.50 per cell). Which is the better buy?

options.t: Pack A, because $12 is less than $15
options.fb: Pack A has a lower total price, but each cell costs $3.00 instead of $2.50.

options.t: Pack B, because $2.50 per cell is less than $3.00 per cell
They cost the same per cell

gates.pass: Pack B saves $0.50 per cell. Beck grabs the 6-pack.

gates.title: Boss Gate · Call the Race
gates.prompt: Compare the final qualifying runs by finding each driver's unit rate.
hints: Conceptual: the driver with more meters per 1 minute is faster.
Procedural: divide each driver's distance by their minutes, then compare.

steps: Driver X: 450 m in 3 min → 450 ÷ 3 = 150 m/min.
Driver Y: 560 m in 4 min → 560 ÷ 4 = 140 m/min.
worked.q: A kart goes 360 meters in 4 minutes. How many meters per minute?

items.label: Viper Red (1,050 m in 5 min) = ___ m/min
items.aria: Viper Red final qualifier unit rate

options.t: Viper Red, because 1,050 meters is farther than 880 meters
options.fb: Farther total distance in more time does not mean faster per minute.

options.t: Zara, because 220 meters per minute beats 210 meters per minute

gates.pass: OFFICIAL: Zara takes pole position at 220 meters per minute!

journal.heading: Lesson 3-2 — what the speed dispute taught us
rows: Compares two amounts with different units, like 600 meters in 3 minutes.
The amount for just 1 unit: 600 ÷ 3 = 200 meters per 1 minute.
Divide total price by number of items to get unit price. Lower unit price wins.
Farther is not faster! Always divide by time before comparing speeds.
journal.quote: "He drove farther, sure, but I drove faster. Math says so." — Spark

teacher.suggested: Use during or after lesson 3-2 (Understand Rates and Unit Rates) as one focused read. Whole-class on a projector, pairs on devices, or independent practice. Covers rate language, finding unit rates by dividing, comparing speeds, and finding better buys.
standards: Understand the concept of a unit rate a/b associated with a ratio a:b with b ≠ 0, and use rate language in the context of a ratio relationship
